title: 前CIA分析师：美国隐蔽行动要总统批，中国国安部却当日常？
speaker: Peter Mattis

segments.en: It explains how the Ministry of State Security operates. How should we think of it kind of in complement with those other intelligence agencies around the world? In some ways, we should kind of
segments.zh: 它解释了国家安全部如何运作。我们该如何将其与全球其他情报机构互补看待？某种程度上，我们可以

segments.en: think of it as being like the old KGB of having a robust domestic mission and the international mission. You know, they collect intelligence the same way that we do the same way that others do,
segments.zh: 将其视为类似旧克格勃，兼具强大的国内和国际任务。他们收集情报的方式与我们和其他人一样，

segments.en: right? They think of of intelligence as activating or catalytic knowledge, right? Information that solves decision-making problems. These are quotes from, from some textbooks. The difference, though,
segments.zh: 对吧？他们认为情报是激活或催化知识，是解决问题的信息。这些是教科书中的引述。然而，不同之处在于，

segments.en: that they have is that they put a lot of effort into what we would call covert action. Something that we consider exceptional or special that requires a presidential finding. In their case, it's something that
segments.zh: 他们大力投入我们所谓的隐蔽行动。我们视为特殊、需要总统批准的行动。对他们来说，这是

segments.en: they consider to be sort of routine, ordinary, you know, just another day that ends and why, so to speak.
segments.zh: 他们认为是例行公事、普通寻常，就像又一天结束一样。

segments.en: And this is not the first kind of tech case where we've seen transfers. And you can kind of get a sense that intelligence is floating in the background, right? Because it's also used as a way to
segments.zh: 这不是我们首次看到技术转移的案例。你能感觉到情报在背景中浮动，因为它也被用来

segments.en: facilitate sort of critical business or strategic business that has a benefit for the Chinese state.
segments.zh: 促进对中国国家有利的关键或战略业务。
